flags.headline: Holding near new 52-week low after CFO disclosed persisting manufacturing constraints
flags.detail: First flagged 2026-09-09 after Stryker CFO Preston Wells (Wells Fargo Healthcare Conference, Sept 8) disclosed peripheral-vascular manufacturing constraints tied to the company's earlier cyber incident now expected to persist into Q4 2026, plus a softer joint-replacement environment. Shares fell ~8.8% that day to a new 52-week low ($276.43) and Wells Fargo cut its price target to $348 from $418. Today shares are roughly flat (-0.33% to $275.52, effectively holding at the new lower level) -- no further deterioration, but no news of resolution either; the underlying operational risk (Q4 manufacturing recovery) has not changed. This is not one of SYK's three listed key_risks in the screener report (forward-multiple/margin-of-safety compression, profit-margin ceiling, hospital-capex sensitivity for Mako) -- worth adding to the next screener refresh as a fourth, newly-materialized risk.

evidence.source: Stryker Investor Relations (2026 Wells Fargo Healthcare Conference webcast notice)

flags.headline: US-Iran conflict near the Strait of Hormuz continues to escalate, unresolved
flags.detail: First flagged 2026-09-06; remains unresolved. A monthlong lull broke in early September and tit-for-tat attacks (US strikes on Iranian tankers, Iranian strikes on tankers and US warships, an IRGC-announced restricted zone near the strait) have continued through this week with no ceasefire or de-escalation reported. Energy-sleeve reaction is mixed today rather than uniformly directional: DVN +1.19% ($48.98), VLO +1.45% ($388.90), CVX +1.82% ($213.80) higher, while OKE -1.67% ($95.86) and CNX -0.74% ($36.75) are lower -- consistent with a market still repricing a live, two-sided geopolitical risk rather than a one-directional flight response. Holding at RED given the unresolved military escalation and DVN's direct oil-price-volatility key_risk exposure.
